title: 15th Sitting of third session of 2025
presiding: Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Speaker); Ahmed Saleem (Deputy Speaker) took the chair partway through the debate
summary: The 15th sitting opened at 09:01 on Tuesday 4 November 2025 with 33 members present, 6 on leave and 5 on official travel, and ended at 10:30 so the whole-house committee could meet at 11:00. The chair announced four committee membership changes, sent the President's nomination of a non-resident ambassador to the Foreign Relations Committee, and read two new items for the first time: a shark-fishing resolution and a bill to repeal the Freedom of Peaceful Assembly Act. Most of the sitting was the preliminary debate on the government's bill to amend the Evidence Act, where members from all sides backed the amendments but argued over the courts, judges and the government's record; the debate was set aside unfinished and a housing resolution on flat and plot handovers was started. The text is readable but some marks are dropped and lines are jumbled, so some details are approximate.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: On the Evidence bill, said the law is already sound and that problems lie with the courts and judges, not the statute.
Rejected the claim that justice goes to those with money and criticised court and Judicial Service Commission changes under this government.
On the housing resolution, said housing is a government duty and budgeted money has not produced flats; asked for quick handover.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Backed the amendments but said judges themselves need reform, citing his roles on the Judicial Service Commission and Judiciary Committee and cases that drag on.
After the chair changed, said main changes cover written, electronic and physical evidence, and urged judges to decide cases fast and fairly.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: On the Evidence bill, said the government's large majority should address the whole justice system, citing the Supreme Court changes and delayed cases.
On the housing resolution, supported it and urged quick handover of plots and flats, including at Gulhifalhu and Giraavaru Falhu.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aslam
positions: As sponsor, said the bill adds digital evidence, rules for witness statements and identification, and press source rules to help serious cases succeed in court.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the amendments, saying major criminal and drug cases fail when evidence is gathered outside the law, and urged committee work to strengthen the bill.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the bill, saying witness evidence is central in Islam and that electronic evidence and press protections should help slow cases move faster.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Supported the bill, citing cases lost over forged documents and mismatched CCTV timestamps, and urged the committee to finish it quickly.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the amendments and said evidence rules must keep large cases from collapsing in court, citing public concern over influence and bribery among judges.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said the government has not delivered on its presidential pledge on detention until trial and criticised its handling of the judiciary and the Judicial Service Commission.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the bill, said evidence is central in Islam, and asked the committee to close loopholes so cases stuck in court can be resolved quickly.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Supported the bill, said the President's influence over courts ended in November 2023, and criticised the previous MDP-led government's judicial record.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Supported the bill, said opposition speeches strayed from it, and welcomed the line-up and prior-statement rules while asking the committee to study technical details.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Defended the government's housing record, said flats and plots are being handed over, and accused MDP members of exaggerating while recalling unfinished projects of past years.

decisions: Four committee membership changes were announced by the chair.
The President's nomination of a non-resident ambassador to Antigua and Barbuda was sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
The minutes of the March 2025 sittings (8 to 10 March) were declared adopted with no amendments.
The shark-fishing resolution and the bill to repeal the Freedom of Peaceful Assembly Act were each read for the first time.
The preliminary debate on the Evidence Act amendment bill was set aside unfinished so the housing resolution could be taken up.
The chair ended the sitting at 10:30 for a whole-house committee meeting at 11:00; the next sitting is on Wednesday 5 November 2025 at 09:00.
